text:
maria_sales: SolaraMed wants a POC next week. Key asks from procurement/netops: agent in their VPC, full client IP visibility in logs, strict egress allowlist (443 + 9000), and a short cost delta for peering vs PrivateLink.

solara_ops: Correct. Also need cert pinning, and can't accept unpredictable egress IPs. Prefer peering if it preserves src IPs.

noah_netops: Peering will preserve source IPs end-to-end if routed correctly. PrivateLink usually terminates at our ENIs; we can avoid SNAT but it depends on connector config. For strict no-SNAT requirement, peering is the safer default.

sara_solutions: High-level tradeoffs to send procurement: peering = preserves src IP, needs route table changes and CIDR checks; PrivateLink = smaller firewall surface (allow to ENI) and simpler for hosted fallbacks but may require extra steps to guarantee src IP.

maria_sales: Can we give them a one-page checklist they can hand to netops + a one-line SOW blurb for each option?

noah_netops: Peering checklist (pasteable):
```
1) Verify CIDR non-overlap (customer: 10.70.0.0/16)
2) Create VPC peering request to Redwood account
3) Accept peering and add route: 10.210.55.0/24 -> peering in customer route tables
4) Security groups: allow outbound tcp ports 443 and 9000 to 10.210.55.0/24
5) Test: curl echo endpoint and confirm X-Client-IP header shows client IP
```

sara_solutions: PrivateLink SG example for fallback:
```
# customer SG
allow tcp from 10.70.0.0/16 to eni-zzzz1111 port 443
allow tcp from 10.70.0.0/16 to eni-zzzz1111 port 9000
```

vivek_security: Security Qs: we support SPKI cert pinning (provide fingerprints), customer-managed KMS for keys at rest on Private deployments, and logs can be forwarded to their SIEM. Default hosted POC log retention is 30 days unless they request otherwise. We'll attach SOC2.

billing-bot: pricing-note: peering + dedicated = committed monthly fee + network egress; hosted + PrivateLink = per-token billing + interface endpoint transfer. Exact numbers need finance sign-off.

maria_sales: Solara wants a 6-week cost estimate (rough) and the runbook. Can we offer a capped trial credit for the POC?

sara_solutions: Yes, offer a capped trial credit and include a non-binding monthly delta estimate line. I'll draft the SOW snippets.

noah_netops: Failover: supported. Recommend primary route via peering, secondary via PrivateLink or EIP-based proxy. We'll include a short failover test and route priority notes.

maria_sales: Can someone add the minimal IAM permissions the customer's admin needs to approve peering and routes? Makes legal review faster.

noah_netops: Minimal IAM list: ec2:CreateVpcPeeringConnection, ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection, ec2:CreateRoute, ec2:ModifyRouteTable, ec2:DescribeVpcs, ec2:DescribeRouteTables.

vivek_security: Also include a note about PII in logs: we'll forward only what they permit and can redact if requested. Add GDPR retention options.

maria_sales: Great. Timeline: need runbook + SG snippets + SOW blurb + pricing note by EOD so procurement can review. Solara aiming to sign after legal on Friday.

billing-bot: task:create solara-peering-runbook assigned to noah_netops ETA 3h

noah_netops: I'll push the draft into this thread in ~2h with test commands (curl + expected headers) and the failover checklist.

sara_solutions: I'll attach the options table and SOW one-liners when Noah posts runbook.

solara_ops: Thanks team  want the quick doc to hand to our network team. Appreciate the fast turnaround.
